access.session.text: start accepts optional session_number to choose an existing slot; without a number it uses the saved session binding; only Legacy admission permits initial slot allocation; an explicit start reuses the old deadline before cooldown and grants a full duration at or after cooldown; end ends the current session and forbids session_number

executor.session.text: attach-only work session lifecycle: action=attach requires a four-digit session_number (leading zeros allowed) and optionally nonblank intent; action=intent requires nonblank intent and forbids session_number; intent refresh keeps the existing attachment

coordinator.session.text: attach-only work session lifecycle: action=attach requires a four-digit session_number (leading zeros allowed) and optionally nonblank intent; action=intent requires nonblank intent and forbids session_number; intent refresh keeps the existing attachment

executor.task_list.text: read is summary-only, excludes archived tasks; state=done includes done tasks; next_cursor continues pagination

coordinator.task_list.text: read is summary-only, excludes archived tasks; state=done includes done tasks; next_cursor continues pagination

*.message.text: send requires non-null text; message_hash must be absent or null. ack requires non-null message_hash; text must be absent or null. reply requires both text and message_hash non-null. read/history/recipients require both text and message_hash absent or null; explicit null is accepted (non-null values forbidden).
Messages use local attachments and expire after 24 hours; scope is always local.
*.message.anchor: this server only. Message recipients require a current local attachment;

*.message.text: For send/reply, nullable mode defaults to notify; mode=alert sets alert and require_reply. Either alert=true or require_reply=true forces final mode=alert even when mode=notify or mode=ack. mode=ack is a delivery mode, distinct from action=ack. Send mode defaults to notify. mode=notify marks read_at automatically on first recipient display, so acknowledged=true means read/handled and does not prove an explicit ACK. mode=ack requires action=ack to set read_at. mode=alert requires a reply to release its reply obligation; action=ack alone does not satisfy it. Either alert=true or require_reply=true promotes notify/ack to alert. first_seen_at records first display; read_at records notify auto-read or explicit ACK; replied_at records actual reply. Repeated ACK is idempotent and creates no new message.
*.message.anchor: normalized_mode = mode or ("alert" if alert or require_reply else "notify")

*.message.text: Local send routes are exclusive: use target=<local public_name> with namespace/task_id absent, OR namespace + task_id together for the task’s current local owners, with target absent/null or broadcast. A partial task pair or a named target combined with a task pair fails input_validation_failed with path/reason/repair hint and outcome=not_committed (no message created). If neither route is specified, the send is a local broadcast (may fail no_active_recipients). reply uses the parent sender and ignores supplied target. For send, missing/null target means local broadcast when no task pair is given.

executor.task_comment.text: comment (default action) requires non-null, non-whitespace comment_text and rejects checkpoint; checkpoint requires non-null checkpoint and rejects comment_text. Unknown fields are forbidden; checkpoint does not accept expected_revision.

executor.task_claim.text: claim requires non-null claim_intent string(1..160) containing non-whitespace characters; runtime trims and rejects whitespace-only intent. claim forbids release_reason; release forbids claim_intent; canonical action-specific field lists apply.

release_reason is optional even when an existing live claim is released: omitted/null uses released_by_owner. A supplied release_reason must be non-whitespace after trimming when a live claim is released; idempotent unclaimed release bypasses reason validation.

coordinator.task_manage.text: create requires non-null isolation_hint. update requires non-null expected_revision (minimum 1) and task_id. For every action the accepted field whitelist, required fields and extra_forbidden policy are compiled from _TASK_MANAGE_MODELS, not from the permissive union.

checkpoint requires non-null checkpoint; state requires non-null state; review requires non-null dimensions (1..3 distinct A/C/R) and verdict; comment requires non-null comment_text with at least one non-whitespace character; relate/unrelate require non-null relation_kind and related_task_id.

archive requires either non-null archive_note or non-null note at canonical model level. Runtime selects raw archive_note if truthy, else note; it then strips and requires non-whitespace text. archive_note="   " masks valid note fallback and fails; supply one meaningful field. create with state=done requires non-null result.

The handler serializes with exclude_none=True and exclude_unset=True; update description:null is omitted/no change, while tags:[] explicitly replaces the stored list with an empty list. Other explicit non-null collection values replace, not append.

relation_kind is an open string(1..64), not an enum. For relation_kind=review_of on relate: source lane must be review; parent candidate_ref must be nonempty; no different review_of parent; source candidate_ref if set must match parent, otherwise it is bound from parent. Possible errors review_task_required, missing_parent_candidate, ambiguous_review_parent, candidate_conflict.
Canonical update/mutation state transitions and task revision checks remain enforced by the existing server; an omitted optional field may mean no mutation.
request_id on create is the stable operation identity; reuse only on transport retries of the same create; independent creates need a fresh request_id.
coordinator.task_manage.anchor: Create operation identity. Reuse only on transport retries

coordinator.task_manage.text: With a live claim, nonowner update permits only safe participant fields title, description, next_action, tags; workflow fields or non-null dependencies require live owner (owner_required). expected_revision is required.
update rejects non-null state and checkpoint; use dedicated state/checkpoint actions.
Non-null update candidate_ref returns candidate_ref_frozen when task is done or has incoming review_of, even for unchanged value; null is omitted.
Admitted nonowners may set workflow state despite a live claim; no content revision CAS check/increment, existing claim unaffected.
When any claim is live, archive, relate and unrelate require the live owner; nonowners get owner_required. Without a live claim this owner gate does not apply.

executor.command_run.text: a command run executes a shell command in the current managed work session; no implicit idempotency guarantee

coordinator.task_get.text: detail chooses snapshot, detail or history; history_kind and cursor apply to history

executor.task_state.text: any admitted agent may set valid workflow state, including on a task claimed by someone else. expected_revision does not guard state writes via content CAS; content revision is unchanged, live claims persist, and repeated state assignment emits no event.

access.get_events.text: event_id and cursor are mutually exclusive; event_id selects one owned event even if already read; without event_id, consume up to limit (1..20) events, ordered oldest first
